name: Tola
overview: Tola is a male figure from the tribe of Issachar, identified as a son of Issachar according to Genesis 46:13. He is listed among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, representing the Tolaites mentioned in Numbers 25:23. His presence in these genealogical records highlights his role within the broader narrative of Israel's early history.
namesAndTitles: The name Tola means "(deep) red, purple," reflecting a proper name recorded in Genesis 46:13. This meaning may suggest a distinctive characteristic or symbolic significance, but the text does not elaborate further on the implications of his name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tola as a son of Issachar. Additional inferred paternal relationships from 1 Chronicles 7:2 include Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Samuel, although these may pertain to different individuals named Tola. Beyond his direct identification as Issachar's son, no further family relationships are definitively established in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tola's importance lies primarily in his genealogical placement among the sons of Israel who migrated to Egypt, marking the foundation of the Israelite nation in a foreign land. As an ancestor of the Tolaites, he represents a tribal lineage within the tribe of Issachar, contributing to the fulfillment of God's promises to Israel. His mention underscores the continuity of God's covenant people through successive generations.
